subject: French (Optional)
content: French greetings are essential for polite conversation. Bonjour (Good morning / Hello - used until evening), Bonsoir (Good evening - used after dark), Salut (Hi - informal, for friends), Bonne nuit (Good night - when going to sleep). Asking how someone is: Comment ça va? (How are you?), Ça va bien, merci (I'm fine, thank you), Et toi? (And you? informal), Et vous? (And you? formal). Introductions: Je m'appelle (My name is...), Comment tu t'appelles? (What is your name? informal), Comment vous appelez-vous? (What is your name? formal), Enchanté(e) (Nice to meet you). Saying goodbye: Au revoir (Goodbye), À bientôt (See you soon), À demain (See you tomorrow), Bonne journée (Have a good day), Bonne soirée (Have a good evening). In Francophone African countries (Benin, Senegal, Ivory Coast, Niger - all neighbours of Nigeria), these greetings are used daily. Learning French opens opportunities in business and travel.
summary: French greetings: Bonjour (hello), Bonsoir (good evening), Salut (hi). Asking: Comment ça va? (How are you?). Introducing: Je m'appelle (My name is). Goodbye: Au revoir, À bientôt.

subject: French (Optional)
content: Learning numbers in French helps with telling time, counting money, and shopping. Numbers 1-10: un (1), deux (2), trois (3), quatre (4), cinq (5), six (6), sept (7), huit (8), neuf (9), dix (10). Numbers 11-20: onze (11), douze (12), treize (13), quatorze (14), quinze (15), seize (16), dix-sept (17), dix-huit (18), dix-neuf (19), vingt (20). Notice patterns: numbers 17-19 combine 'dix' (10) with 7-9. To say your age: J'ai ... ans (I am ... years old). Example: J'ai dix ans (I am 10 years old). To ask age: Quel âge as-tu? (How old are you?) In Nigerian markets near Benin border, knowing French numbers helps with bargaining. Practice counting objects in French.
summary: French numbers 1-20: un, deux, trois, quatre, cinq, six, sept, huit, neuf, dix, onze, douze, treize, quatorze, quinze, seize, dix-sept, dix-huit, dix-neuf, vingt.

subject: French (Optional)
content: Colors (les couleurs) in French: rouge (red), bleu (blue), jaune (yellow), vert (green), orange (orange), violet (purple), rose (pink), marron (brown), noir (black), blanc (white), gris (grey). Note: colors agree with the noun they describe (feminine/masculine). Example: un stylo rouge (a red pen - masculine), une fleur rouge (a red flower - feminine). Shapes (les formes): cercle (circle), carré (square), triangle (triangle), rectangle (rectangle), ovale (oval), étoile (star), cœur (heart). Describing objects: C'est un cercle rouge (It's a red circle), C'est un carré bleu (It's a blue square). In French-speaking West Africa, knowing colors helps describe clothing in markets (une robe rouge - red dress, un t-shirt bleu - blue t-shirt). Colors are also used in art class and describing flags (le drapeau du Nigeria est vert, blanc, vert - Nigeria's flag is green, white, green).
summary: French colors: rouge (red), bleu (blue), jaune (yellow), vert (green), noir (black), blanc (white). Shapes: cercle (circle), carré (square), triangle (triangle), rectangle (rectangle).

subject: French (Optional)
content: Family vocabulary in French helps you talk about your loved ones. La famille (family). Members: mère (mother), père (father), frère (brother), sœur (sister), grand-mère (grandmother), grand-père (grandfather), tante (aunt), oncle (uncle), cousin (cousin - male), cousine (cousin - female), bébé (baby). Using possessive: ma mère (my mother - feminine), mon père (my father - masculine), mes parents (my parents - plural). Talking about family: J'ai une sœur (I have one sister), J'ai deux frères (I have two brothers), C'est ma grand-mère (This is my grandmother). In Francophone Africa, family is very important, and extended family often lives together. Practice: draw your family tree and label members in French.
summary: Family in French: mère (mother), père (father), frère (brother), sœur (sister), grand-mère (grandmother), grand-père (grandfather), tante (aunt), oncle (uncle), cousin/cousine.

subject: French (Optional)
content: Days of the week in French: lundi (Monday), mardi (Tuesday), mercredi (Wednesday), jeudi (Thursday), vendredi (Friday), samedi (Saturday), dimanche (Sunday). Months of the year: janvier (January), février (February), mars (March), avril (April), mai (May), juin (June), juillet (July), août (August), septembre (September), octobre (October), novembre (November), décembre (December). Useful phrases: Quel jour sommes-nous? (What day is it?), Nous sommes lundi (It's Monday). Quelle est la date aujourd'hui? (What is today's date?), Aujourd'hui c'est le premier janvier (Today is January 1st). On ne travaille pas le dimanche (We don't work on Sunday - many countries observe Sunday rest). In Francophone Africa, the work week is Monday-Friday, with Saturday half-day in some places. Days are not capitalized in French unless starting a sentence.
summary: French days: lundi (Monday), mardi (Tuesday), mercredi (Wednesday), jeudi (Thursday), vendredi (Friday), samedi (Saturday), dimanche (Sunday). Months: janvier to décembre.
